title: Can two people have the same IP address?
sources: IETF RFC 1918 Address Allocation for Private Internets

lines.text: Every computer on the internet has an IP address, but can two different people share the exact same one?
lines.caps: Can two people *share | the exact same *IP address?

lines.text: The answer is yes, and millions of people do every single day.
lines.caps: The answer is *yes | and millions do every *day!

lines.text: Inside private local networks, almost every home router assigns devices addresses like 192.168.1.1.
lines.caps: Local routers use standard *private | internal IP *addresses

lines.text: Millions of people share those private internal IP addresses without conflict.
When heading onto the public internet, a process called Network Address Translation converts all your family's devices to one public IP.
lines.caps: Your router groups all *family | devices into one *public IP

lines.text: Mobile phone carriers also use Carrier-Grade NAT, bundling thousands of different cellular users under a single public IP address.
lines.caps: Cellular carriers bundle *thousands | of phones under *one IP!

lines.text: Your IP address is more like a shared apartment lobby than a single private bedroom.
lines.caps: An IP is like a shared *lobby | rather than a private *room!
